title: Wall Street Giant Charles Schwab Dips Toes into Prediction Markets with S&P 500 Wagers
summary:
Financial services giant Charles Schwab is reportedly making a surprising entry into the prediction markets, offering customers simple yes-or-no bets on the S&P 500's closing price.
This move by a mainstream institution signals a significant step towards legitimizing and potentially mainstreaming prediction markets within traditional finance.
content:
Get ready to place your bets, but perhaps not in the way you'd expect from your typical brokerage account. Charles Schwab, a name synonymous with prudent, mainstream investing, is reportedly making a surprising foray into the burgeoning world of prediction markets.

According to a recent Wall Street Journal report, the financial services titan plans to introduce a new offering allowing customers to make simple yes-or-no wagers on the S&P 500. Forget complex derivatives or intricate algorithms; this initiative zeroes in on straightforward bets: will the benchmark index close above or below a predetermined target price?

This move isn't just a new product launch; it's a significant signal. For a legacy institution like Schwab to step into a space often associated with fringe finance or speculative trading lends a powerful sense of legitimacy to prediction markets. It suggests that these novel instruments, which allow participants to wager on future events and collectively aggregate probabilities, are moving closer to mainstream acceptance.

While the initial offering appears designed for simplicity, targeting perhaps a broader base of investors looking for novel engagement with market trends, its long-term implications are far-reaching. Could this open the floodgates for other major brokerages to explore similar offerings, potentially revolutionizing how everyday investors interact with market forecasts and event probabilities? Schwab's cautious yet deliberate entry could very well be a bellwether for the future of retail finance.
keyTakeaways: Charles Schwab is reportedly entering prediction markets, a move that could significantly impact the financial industry.
Their initial offering will focus on simple yes-or-no wagers regarding whether the S&P 500 closes above or below a target price.
This entry by a major, traditional financial institution like Schwab signals increased legitimization and potential mainstream adoption for prediction markets.
author: Turner Wright

title: SmackDown Set to Explode: Rhodes vs. Gunther, Zayn Referees, and Tournament Chaos Awaits
summary: Tonight's WWE SmackDown presents a highly anticipated clash between Cody Rhodes and Gunther, with Sami Zayn serving as special guest referee, adding an unpredictable dynamic. The episode also features critical King and Queen of the Ring semi-final matches, setting the stage for future championship contenders.
content:
Tonight's WWE SmackDown promises to be more than just another stop on the road to a major pay-per-view. It's shaping up to be a pivotal night, highlighted by an extraordinary encounter: "The American Nightmare" Cody Rhodes squares off against the formidable Intercontinental Champion, Gunther. This isn't just a marquee match; it's a clash of titans with high personal stakes, elevated further by the surprising appointment of Sami Zayn as the special guest referee.

The showdown between Rhodes and Gunther rekindles a rivalry steeped in their epic 2023 Royal Rumble confrontation, where Gunther outlasted Rhodes for a record-breaking performance. While no championship is on the line tonight, the implications are immense for both competitors. Rhodes, still chasing the elusive world title, needs to prove he can overcome any challenge, even one as dominant as Gunther. For the Ring General, a victory over a top-tier contender like Rhodes would only solidify his already legendary reign and formidable presence on the blue brand. This non-title bout could very well be a preview of future championship gold clashes.

Adding a layer of unpredictable drama is Sami Zayn's special referee role. Zayn, a fan-favorite known for his unwavering moral compass but also his history of getting entangled in chaotic narratives, brings an intriguing wildcard element. Will he maintain impartiality, or will his presence inadvertently — or intentionally — sway the outcome? Meanwhile, the night also features the crucial semi-final matches of both the King and Queen of the Ring tournaments. These bouts are designed to elevate new contenders, offering the winners not just a crown, but a direct path to a world championship opportunity, making every move on the path to the finals critically important.

With such a stacked card, SmackDown is poised to deliver a night of intense competition and potentially narrative-altering moments. From the high-stakes main event with its enigmatic referee to the crowning of tournament finalists, viewers are in for a compelling broadcast that could significantly reshape the landscape of WWE’s premier championships and rivalries.
keyTakeaways: Cody Rhodes faces Gunther in a high-stakes non-title match, rekindling their 2023 Royal Rumble rivalry.
Sami Zayn's role as special guest referee introduces an unpredictable element to the main event's outcome.
The King and Queen of the Ring semi-finals will determine finalists who earn future world championship opportunities.
author: El Presidente

title: AMD Reverses Course: Ryzen 9000 CPUs to Regain Critical Memory Encryption Feature Next Month
summary: AMD is reinstating its Transparent Secure Memory Encryption (TSME) feature on non-PRO Ryzen 9000 desktop CPUs through a BIOS update arriving in July. This crucial security capability, which was initially removed, is returning due to significant community feedback, safeguarding user data at a hardware level.
content:
In a move that underscores the power of user feedback, AMD has announced it will reinstate Transparent Secure Memory Encryption (TSME) on its non-PRO Ryzen 9000 desktop processors this July. This essential security feature, designed to protect sensitive data in memory, makes a welcome return after its unexpected absence caused a stir among the enthusiast community.

TSME, often branded as 'Memory Guard' in AMD's PRO lineup, provides hardware-level encryption for system memory. This means data is encrypted as it moves through the system, offering a robust shield against sophisticated attacks like cold boot attacks or physical memory tampering. Its initial removal from the mainstream Ryzen 9000 chips, which include some of AMD’s most powerful CPUs, was a peculiar decision that left many users concerned about the platform's security posture.

Fortunately, AMD appears to have listened intently to the chorus of voices from its user base and hardware critics. The company explicitly cited "valuable community feedback" as the driving force behind this reinstatement. It's a clear signal that the chipmaker is committed to both performance and security, recognizing that advanced hardware demands comprehensive protection.

The reintroduction of TSME will arrive via a routine BIOS update, making it accessible to all eligible Ryzen 9000 desktop users. This proactive step not only restores a critical layer of defense but also reinforces AMD's dedication to supporting the long-term integrity and security of its platforms. For users, it means an enhanced peace of mind, knowing their data is better secured at the foundation of their PC.
keyTakeaways: AMD is bringing back Transparent Secure Memory Encryption (TSME) to non-PRO Ryzen 9000 desktop CPUs.
The reinstatement, due in July via a BIOS update, is a direct response to 'valuable community feedback'.
TSME is a vital hardware-level security feature that encrypts system memory, protecting against advanced data theft and physical attacks.
author: Jake Roach

title: Forget Rebooting: Your Motherboard Can Transform That Old Reset Button into a Powerhouse
summary: The once-essential PC reset button is largely obsolete in modern systems due to stable OS and fast SSDs, leading many new cases to omit it. However, modern motherboards are ingeniously repurposing this dormant physical input, allowing users to remap it for various functions like RGB control, fan speed adjustments, or even direct BIOS access.
content:
Remember the PC reset button? For decades, it was a ubiquitous presence on computer cases, a quick, albeit sometimes drastic, fix for a frozen system. But in an era of lightning-fast SSDs and increasingly stable operating systems, that dedicated reboot method has quietly faded into obscurity. Many modern chassis don't even bother including one, viewing it as an unnecessary relic of a bygone era.

Yet, even if your case *does* have this physical relic, chances are it sits dormant, an unused port to a functionality you rarely, if ever, need. This isn't just about nostalgia; it’s about a valuable, tactile input left untapped. Fortunately, motherboard manufacturers, ever keen on extracting maximum utility from every component, are stepping in to give this obsolete button a surprising second life.

Modern motherboards are increasingly offering the ability to repurpose that old reset switch, transforming it from a simple "off-and-on-again" trigger into a versatile command center. Imagine pressing a physical button to cycle through your RGB lighting profiles, instantly adjust fan speeds for quiet operation or maximum cooling, or even trigger a safe boot directly into your BIOS settings.

The possibilities extend further. Some boards allow it to initiate a direct power cycle, bypassing software altogether, or even run custom scripts for advanced users. It's a brilliant blend of old-school physical control and cutting-edge customization, turning a forgotten feature into a direct line to your system's core functions. This ingenuity reclaims valuable case real estate and offers PC enthusiasts a new level of immediate, physical command over their build.

So, while the reset button may be dead in its original form, its spirit, and indeed its physical presence, are being resurrected. It’s a testament to how even the most mundane components can find renewed relevance through clever design, giving users more control and convenience than ever before.
keyTakeaways: The traditional PC reset button is becoming obsolete as operating systems stabilize and SSDs make reboots quick.
Many modern PC cases no longer include a dedicated reset button, rendering any existing ones dormant.
New motherboards offer a clever solution, allowing users to repurpose the reset button for custom functions like RGB control, fan speed, or direct BIOS access.
author: Rich Edmonds
